release_rule: No entry below 'reviewed' may be shown to a participant. Fill 'missing' with a first-language reviewer, then raise each status.
warning: Every consent-specific term is still missing. Nothing here may be shown to a participant until a first-language reviewer has filled the gaps and raised each status to 'reviewed'.
notes: The source PDF is a scan with no text layer. All 93 pages were rasterised at 180 dpi and read with tesseract. The OCR is good on the two-column phrase pages and drifts by one row on the A-Z glossary pages, where a headword can pick up the translation of the line above or below.

Because of that drift, nothing was taken from the glossary alone unless a phrase elsewhere in the book confirmed it. Three glossary lines that looked right were rejected on that test: 'Stop = Sintolo' (that is 'Store'), 'Thank = Lilete' (that is 'Testicle') and 'Trust = Habeli' (that is 'Twice').

This is the best-covered of the four scanned or learner sources: 30 of 53 ids, and it is the only language in the pack with a confirmed word for 'witness' (Paki), which the non-reader consent path needs.
Silozi is a Bantu language with noun classes; single-word glosses change shape inside a sentence.
Several words carry the letter n-with-tilde (ñ). OCR renders it unreliably, so 'mañi' and 'kabakalañi' in particular should be checked against print.

t.yes.note: Corroborated twice in the phrase sections: 'Eni, President u ñozi libuka' and 'Eni sha, kubala kwa katulusa' = yes indeed.

t.no.note: 'Batili, ni hanyinyani' = no, not at all. The glossary's own 'No' line is an OCR column slip and was not used.

t.thank_you.note: 'Ni kandelezi hahulu, ni itumezi' = thank you very much; 'Lu itumezi hahulu-hulu' = thank you very much indeed.

t.please.note: Silozi has no separate word for please. Politeness is the 'Amu-' polite imperative: 'Amu bize ŋaka' = please call the doctor, 'Amu teeleze' = please listen. The consent screens should use this form, not a word.

t.sick.note: 'Komu yaka ya kula' = my cow is sick; 'Ya kula ki mañi?' = who is sick.

t.where_hurt.note: Directly attested: 'where exactly do you feel pain'. 'Mwa utwa butuku fa?' = does it hurt here. 'butuku' = pain.

t.clinic.note: 'Sipatela si fakaufi nji?' = is the hospital near. The glossary's clinic line did not survive OCR; sipatela covers hospital and is the safe word.

t.water.note: Glossary and phrases agree: 'Likubu ni zona li pila mwa mezi' = hippos also live in the water.

t.child.note: Plural 'Banana'. 'Mwanana u i kolofalize maswe' = the child has hurt herself badly.

t.parent_guardian.note: 'Mushemi wa muuna, ndate' = father; 'Boma' = your mother. 'Mushemi' is the parent word. There is no sourced term for a legal guardian.

t.person.note: 'Ki mutu yomunde' = he is a good person; 'Batu ba bañata' = most people.

t.witness.note: Glossary 'Witness = Paki', corroborated by 'Eye-witness = Paki ya iponezi ze eza'. This is the only language in the pack with a confirmed word for witness, which matters for the non-reader consent path.

t.question.note: Glossary 'Question = Puzo, kubuza'; 'kubuza' = to ask is corroborated in the idiom section.

t.read_aloud.note: 'Mu ya lata kubala libuka?' = do you enjoy reading books. The 'aloud' half is not sourced; pair it with the Amu- polite imperative.

t.listen.note: 'Amu teeleze (teeleza)' = listen; 'Ni bata kuteeleza kwa wayalesi' = I want to listen to the radio.

t.do_you_understand.note: Glossary 'Understand = Kuutwisisa'. The question form is reconstructed; confirm.

t.dont_know.note: Built from 'Ziba, kuziba' = to know. Confirm the negative form.

t.confidential.note: Glossary 'Secret = Kunutu'. Secrecy is not the same as research confidentiality; a reviewer must decide whether this is the right word for a consent form.

t.withdraw.note: 'ni mu eleza kutuhela kuca' = I advised him to stop eating. This is 'to stop', not the legal sense of withdrawing consent.

t.stop_any_time.en: You can stop at any time
t.stop_any_time.note: Built from 'kutuhela' = to stop and 'nako kaufela' = always/at all times, both attested separately. The sentence itself is NOT sourced.

t.payment.note: 'U palelwa kulifa nji?' = are you not able to pay. 'mali' = money.

t.not_paid.note: Built from 'kulifa'. Not a sourced sentence.

t.language.note: Plural 'Lipuwo'. From the book's own contents page: 'Lipuwo / Mishobo = Languages, Tribes'.

t.age.note: 'Nawa u na ni lilimo ze kai?' = how old is Nawa; literally 'how many years does Nawa have'.

t.who.note: 'Ya kula ki mañi?' = who is sick; 'Ya mu holofalize ki mañi?' = who hurt him.

t.what.note: 'Mina mu katazwa kini?' = what is wrong with you.

t.where.note: 'Mukuli u inzi kai?' = where is the patient.

t.when.note: 'Sipatela se si yahilwe lili?' = when was this hospital built.

t.why.note: The glossary's 'Why?' line did not survive OCR. This is the standard form; confirm.
